subject: SUM function
notes: PARTIAL -> CONFORMS 2026-09-05 (kb/Work PB252). THE PRIOR RECORD'S OWN LANE (b) DESCRIPTION WAS WRONG, and that is what this landing corrects. It read: '`case "SumScaled" or "RangeScaled"` takes AlignedArgs ... and calls CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SumScaled (`Int128 s = 0; foreach (x) s += x`) ... the alignment is escape-checked (CobolNum.RescaleEscape), so an argument that cannot be represented in the Int128 intermediate raises the size-error condition instead of wrapping.' RescaleEscape bounds each ALIGNED ARGUMENT and says nothing about their SUM: `Int128.Abs(value) > Int128.MaxValue / Pow10Wide(toScale - fromScale)`. MEASURED on the compiler's own exe before the fix, inside the 31-digit cap: `P PIC S9(31) VALUE ALL '9'` beside `Q PIC SV9(7)`, `COMPUTE R = FUNCTION SUM(P P P Q) ON SIZE ERROR ...` -- each aligned argument (9.99e37) passes the per-argument bound (1.70e31 at scale 7), their sum 2.9999e38 exceeds Int128.MaxValue and wrapped to -4.028e37, which at scale 7 fits a 31-digit receiver, so the phrase was NOT taken and a SIGN-FLIPPED value was stored silently. The EAE's true value (3x10^31 - 3) needs 32 digits, so Sec.14.7.5 rule 3 makes the size error condition exist there with NO implementor latitude at all. FIX: the accumulator is now `checked` under one try for the whole loop and escapes through CobolIntrinsics.Exact.cs#SizeEscape -> CobolSizeError/EC-SIZE-OVERFLOW, which ArithmeticEmitter lands on the ON SIZE ERROR arm leaving the receiver unchanged (Sec.14.7.5 rule 1). GOVERNING CLAUSE CORRECTED IN THE SAME CHANGE: the message text had carried PB32's inherited 'ISO Sec.8.8.1.2 rule 7', which is a REAL clause answering a DIFFERENT question (arithmetic expressions are exempt from the composite-of-operands limit); the rule that makes this the size error condition is Sec.14.7.5 rule 5 -- 'if native arithmetic is in effect and the implementor defines that the range of values allowed for the intermediate data item is to be checked, when an arithmetic operation on the intermediate data item would cause the new value to be outside of the allowed range' (--check 14.7.5 -> OK). ALL THREE LANES NOW READ AND EACH IS THE Sec.15.88.4 r1 EAE: (a) standard modes -> SumDec on the SDIDI, left to right; (b) NATIVE fixed-point -> the checked Int128 accumulator, exact until the D1 boundary and then LOUD; (c) NATIVE with a float argument -> SumReal. Left-to-right accumulation is normative (Sec.8.8.1.2 rule 3, --check OK), so a partial sum that escapes the carrier IS an r5 size error even when later terms would bring the total back inside -- the modular cancellation the old unchecked `s += x` happened to deliver was two's complement's answer, not the standard's. CLOSING EVIDENCE: conformance:cases/15.76.4-Returned-value-rule/pb252_native_carrier_boundary pins the r3 case (no latitude) and a control well inside the carrier; the drift test closes the whole exact-carrier entry-point set by reflection, so a new variadic exact function cannot ship unguarded. Both were verified to FAIL on the pre-fix build (SUM-R3-SIZE-ERROR=NO, RANGE-SIGN=NEGATIVE). EDITIONS: carried forward as adjudicated; the witness itself needs 31-digit items so it lives in the 2002 corpus (COBOL-85 caps fixed-point at 18 digits, COBOL0802).
